To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the meaA gene encodes a novel vitamin-B _{12} -dependent enzyme that is required for the utilization of acetyl-CoA as a carbon source.

a protein with similarity to methylmalonyl CoA mutase is essential for the conversion of acetyl CoA to glyoxalate and that this enzyme is probably involved in the metabolism of ethanol and methanol in Methylobacter extorquens.

a protein having similarity to methylmalonyl-coenzyme A mutase is required in Methylobacter extorquens for the assimilation (conversion into cell material) of methanol and that a protein with similarity to a 3-oxacyl-acyl-carrier protein reductase is not essential for this conversion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the genes required for the assimilatory conversion of methanol and/or ethanol to CO2 and H2O in Methylobacter AM1, a facultative methylotroph.
the assimilation of carbon compounds in bacteria.
the elucidation of the genetic basis for the conversion of acetyl-CoA into glyoxylate, which is the first step in the assimilation pathway for methanol and ethanol.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
meaA encodes a vitamin-B12-dependent protein that is required for growth on methonol and ethanol, and the gene product is similar to methylmalonyl CoA mutase.

a protein having similarity to methylmalonyl CoA mutase is essential for the conversion of acetyl CoA to glyoxalate and is required for the growth of M. extorquens on methanol and ethanol, but it is not a methylmalonylCoA mutase.
the meaA gene is required for the growth of Methylobacteria on methanol and ethanol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assimilation of ethanol and methanol requires at least four enzymes, two of which have been identified.
a methylmalonyl CoA mutase-like protein is essential for the assimilation, but not the oxidation, of methanol and that it does not catalyse the conversion of methylmalonyl-coenzyme A to succinate.
the meaA gene is involved in the assimilation, but not the dissimilation, of methanol and is essential for growth on ethanol, and that the meaB gene may be involved in the dissimilation of methanol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the meaA gene is essential for the growth on methanol and ethanol in M. extorquens.
the methylmalonyl CoA mutase gene in M. extorquens is required for the utilization of acetyl-CoA, and therefore methanol and ethanol, as the sole carbon source.
the meaA gene, which is involved in the assimilation and metabolism of methanol and other C1 compounds by M. extorquens, is not methylmalonyl-coenzyme A mutase.
